name: binsider
why: A TUI for poking at ELF binaries, dependencies and strings, a solid entry point into binary exploration.

brief.what_it_is: Binsider is a terminal user interface (TUI) for analyzing ELF binaries, the executable format used on most Linux systems. You point it at a binary and it shows general file info (size, ownership, permissions, date) and linked shared libraries, the ELF layout (sections, segments, symbols, relocations), strings, and a hexdump, with an option to execute the binary and trace its system calls and signals. Input is a binary file path; output is an interactive terminal view rather than a text report. The homepage describes it as offering features similar to readelf and strace.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to get inside ELF binaries with one tool: static and dynamic analysis, strings, linked libraries and hexdumps, all in a user-friendly terminal interface. The project tagline is "Swiss army knife for reverse engineers."
brief.how_it_works: Static analysis parses the ELF structure and lets you navigate sections, segments, symbols and relocations. Dynamic analysis executes the binary and traces system calls, signals and execution flow, similar to strace and ltrace. String extraction works like strings(1) and is aimed at finding things like URLs or passwords; the hexdump view gives a structured look at raw bytes.

commands_seen.context: Quickstart install method from the README, using Cargo (the Rust package manager). Other install methods are linked from the docs at binsider.dev/installation/other/.
Quickstart command to open a binary in the TUI. The placeholder <binary> is the path to the ELF file to analyze.

brief.install_notes: Quickstart is cargo install binsider; the README says that after installation you are "pretty much set." Other methods are listed in the docs, and the README mentions a Docker image (orhunp/binsider) and a crates.io package. Brew is the route the catalogue entry uses. Nothing in the README calls for extra accounts, hardware or configuration.
brief.standout: It bundles what would otherwise be several separate tools (stat/ldd, readelf, strings, strace/ltrace, xxd-style hexdump) into one interactive TUI, which is a different shape from the one-shot text output of those utilities.
brief.status: Likely maintained, but unverified. The GitHub page I read showed CI, CD, Docker and docs.rs badges and an active Discord, but it did not show a release date or last commit date, so I cannot confirm recent activity from what I fetched.
brief.caveats: The project is aimed at ELF binaries, so it will not help with PE or Mach-O files. Dynamic analysis runs the target binary, so it should be used with care on untrusted samples. Licensed under either Apache-2.0 or MIT at the user's option. The README says the copyright is 2024 by Orhun Parmaksız. The docs site was not read beyond the homepage and README.
